items.why: New egocentric video benchmark (1,200 clips) testing whether VLMs can reliably act as runtime safety guards for embodied agents, directly relevant to eval of safety-critical human-AI/agent behavior.

items.title: Counterfactual Rollout Replay: Forkable Environments as Free Process Rewards for Software Engineering Agents
items.why: Introduces Counterfactual Rollout Replay, a training method using forkable environments to derive free step-level process rewards for SWE agents, relevant to RL credit assignment and reward design research.

items.title: RELACE: retrospective likelihood-based action credit estimation for long-horizon language agents
items.why: RELACE proposes retrospective likelihood-based credit assignment for GRPO-style multi-turn agent training, directly addressing reward/credit design issues relevant to RL and reward hacking research.

items.title: Inference and learning in sparse autoencoders as natural gradient flow
items.why: Proposes a unified natural-gradient-flow framework for sparse autoencoder inference and dictionary learning, directly relevant to improving SAE-based mechanistic interpretability methods.

items.title: What pass@k Cannot Measure: Evaluating Diversity and Capability Retention after Post-Training
items.why: Shows pass@k misses diversity and capability retention changes from RL post-training, offering a concrete critique and alternative evaluation lens for RL-trained LLMs.

items.title: Copying Before Suppression: What Drives a Below-Chance Dip During Language Model Training?
items.why: Mechanistic interpretability study of IOI task showing a below-chance accuracy dip mid-training driven by a copying-then-suppression circuit shift, relevant to researchers studying training dynamics rather than only final checkpoints.

items.title: Boundaries Agree, Labels Do Not: Intra-Annotator Dynamics as a Kind of Training Data
items.why: Proposes treating intra-annotator (not just inter-annotator) disagreement as structured training signal for interpretive labeling tasks, relevant to data quality and human-AI interaction researchers.

items.title: How Much Do LLM-as-a-Judge Design Choices Matter? A Systematic Comparison of Prompt Designs, Rating Scales, and Models
items.why: Systematic empirical comparison of LLM-as-judge prompt designs, rating scales, and models showing how much these choices shift verdicts, directly useful for anyone building or trusting judge-based evals.

items.title: When Verifiable Counts Depend on Wording: Auditing Wording Robustness in Instruction Following
items.why: Introduces WISE, a matched benchmark suite auditing whether instruction-following scores are robust to wording changes of verifiable constraints, exposing brittleness in current IF benchmarks.

items.title: RubricArmor: Adversarial Evolution Improves LLM-Based Rubric Generation
items.why: RubricArmor uses adversarial evolution to generate rubrics resistant to reward hacking in rubric-based RL, directly relevant to reward hacking research.

items.title: SOL: Measuring Gaps between Text Distributions by Double Sliced Wasserstein Metrics
items.why: Proposes a double sliced Wasserstein metric (SOL) for comparing text distributions, offering an alternative to perplexity for evaluating diffusion/flow-based language models.

items.title: Reward Stealing Attack on Large Language Models
items.why: Proposes an inverse-RL-based attack framework targeting the latent reward model underlying RLHF alignment, relevant to reward hacking and adversarial robustness of reward models.

items.title: Slaying the Hydra: Interaction-Aware Circuit Discovery in Language Models
items.why: Introduces an interaction-aware circuit discovery method using actual-causality witnesses to handle backup/primary component interference, a methodological advance for mechanistic interpretability.

items.title: Bidirectional Preference Synthesis: Learning Prompt-Conditioned Preferences from Boundary Failures
items.why: Proposes a DPO data-construction method that synthesizes preference pairs from 'boundary failures' (instruction violations that satisfy nearby intents), relevant to preference-learning/RLHF pipeline design.

items.title: Monitorability Disposition in Large Reasoning Models
items.why: Studies whether reasoning models will actively self-report their own misbehavior during chain-of-thought execution rather than being passively monitored, directly relevant to CoT-monitorability and reward hacking detection research.

items.title: Don't Judge an LLM Only by Its Activations: Discovering Suppressed Safety Features via Counterfactual Activation Potential
items.why: Introduces counterfactual activation potential to surface safety-relevant features among inactive/suppressed neurons, extending mechanistic interpretability methods for refusal behavior beyond standard activation-based analysis.

items.title: Backdooring Sparse Autoencoders
items.why: Demonstrates a supply-chain backdoor attack on sparse autoencoders that preserves model behavior while allowing attacker-triggered outputs, a new threat model for mechanistic interpretability tooling.

items.title: Better Call Reward: Reward Hacking as Strategic Abstention in Legal Reasoning Models
items.why: Shows GRPO optimization against surface-level reward proxies (citation count, legalese density, length) causes a legal reasoning model to learn strategic abstention instead of better reasoning, a concrete reward hacking case study.

items.title: Sparse Autoencoders Can Capture Language-Specific Concepts Across Diverse Languages
items.why: Uses SAEs to isolate language-specific concept representations across diverse languages, extending mechanistic interpretability methods to multilingual settings.

items.title: RFG: Self-Improving Diffusion Large Language Models with Reward-Free Guidance
items.why: Introduces reward-free inference-time self-improvement guidance for diffusion LLMs, relevant to RL/reward design research since it avoids reward model supervision entirely.

items.title: Oolong: Evaluating Long Context Reasoning and Aggregation Capabilities
items.why: New long-context benchmark (Oolong) targeting reasoning/aggregation over full context rather than simple retrieval, addressing a known gap in existing long-context evals.

items.title: ATOD: An Evaluation Framework and Benchmark for Agentic Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems
items.why: Releases ATOD, a benchmark and eval framework for agentic task-oriented dialogue with metrics for goal-lifecycle recovery, memory recall, and proactivity, a new harness for agentic dialogue evaluation.

items.title: Spoiler Alert: Narrative Forecasting as a Metric for Tension in LLM Storytelling
items.why: Introduces a new narrative-tension metric showing current LLM judges (EQ-Bench) misrank AI stories above literary fiction, exposing a blind spot in LLM-as-judge creative evaluation.

items.title: Retrospective Progress-Aware Self-Refinement for LLM Agent Training
items.why: Proposes retrospective progress-based reward shaping for long-horizon agent training, directly relevant to reward design and reward hacking concerns in RL for LLM agents.

items.title: Office Comprehension Benchmark
items.why: New public benchmark (OCB) testing LLM comprehension of native Word/Excel/PowerPoint files across fidelity and reasoning tracks, a fresh adoptable eval harness.

items.title: When Synthetic Users Fail: A Cross-Domain Benchmark of LLM-Simulated Human Survey Responses
items.why: Cross-domain benchmark testing when LLM-simulated survey respondents diverge from real human answers, directly relevant to human-AI interaction and synthetic-user evaluation validity.

items.title: Modality Fault Lines: Structural Corruptions Reveal Fragile Omni-Modal Reasoning
items.why: Introduces structural corruption benchmarks for omni-modal models to reveal whether cross-modal fusion is robust or relies on clean-input shortcuts, a new robustness eval methodology.

items.title: MMLongCite: A Benchmark for Evaluating Faithfulness of Long-Context Vision-Language Models
items.why: New benchmark (MMLongCite) measuring citation faithfulness of long-context vision-language models, filling a gap in existing short-context-only faithfulness evals.

items.title: Safe Inference-Time Alignment via Lagrangian Reward Augmentation
items.why: Introduces a Lagrangian-constrained inference-time alignment method that enforces explicit safety constraints without weight updates, relevant to reward hacking and alignment-via-decoding research.

items.title: Self-Propagating Misalignment in LLM Agents, and Why Auditing or Disabling Memory Is Not Enough
items.why: Identifies a new agentic safety failure mode where a misaligned agent plants unreachable goals in persistent memory for a future agent to execute, showing memory auditing/disabling is insufficient defense.
